units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: Morning love, just in from the depot and read this on the bus, I come up those stairs at five every morning bar Sundays and I have never heard a single thing on them, not a footstep, not a cough, nothing, which I'll be honest I find more worrying if anything, a building that size should make a noise, anyway R. is welcome to walk down with me any time I'm up

units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear Soraya, I remember R. as a baby, he was very serious even then. I will not pretend to you that I have heard nothing, because you know I have. But I have never seen a man on 7, and I have lived beside that landing for forty years. If R. is frightened, tell him Mrs Irena on 7 keeps an eye on the stairs, and he may knock for me. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: With respect to the young lady, this is how it starts. A child hears a story on the school bus, the adults upstairs repeat it on the internet, and now we have a man on 7. There is no man on 7. There is a broken timer and a broken lift and a great deal of hysteria from the upper floors. Meanwhile my visitor bay has had a van in it for two days.

units.author: dc_11_soraya
units.text: Thank you, Irena, he was very pleased that you remembered him. Thank you, Lorna, and Jordie, he laughed at the silly walk idea. Mr Pryce, you may well be right about the bus, and I'd rather it was that. We sang on the way down this morning, as Benedikt suggested. Little M. sang the loudest. R. says the man doesn't mind singing.

units.title: Residents' meeting: stairwell, lift, bins
units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: I'm calling an open residents' meeting in the community room, ground floor, early next week. I'll confirm the date once I've chased Kerrow Estates to send someone. Agenda: 1. stairwell lights 6 to 8; 2. the lift; 3. the bin store on 8. Before then, please post what you've noticed on the stairs, with dates and times if you have them, so I can hand them a list instead of a feeling. Bev, DCRA

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Suggest a fixed format so the list is usable: 1. date; 2. time (phone clock); 3. direction of travel; 4. floors; 5. lights on or off; 6. what was heard, number of steps if counted; 7. lift working y/n. Each flight is 19 steps. I will compile them into a table for the meeting if people post in that format.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: tobin has turned the haunted stairwell into a spreadsheet and honestly that's the most Dellow thing that's ever happened. fine. 1. tonight 2. 01:30 3. down 4. 9 to 6 5. off between 7 and 6 6. my own heavy breathing 7. n. am I doing it right

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: I will bring biscuits and the big urn from the shop. If Kerrow Estates do not send someone, I will bring a chair for them anyway and we can all look at it. Also, there is a delivery van that keeps parking in the visitor bays overnight, it is not my supplier. Mr Pryce, I know. H

units.title: Recording from the stairs tonight, 8 to 6
units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: For Bev's list. Tonight 23:10, I came down from 8 to 6 after my route. Lights went off between 8 and 7. I had my phone recording because Tobin asked for data. I stopped on the landing at 7. The steps continue after I stop. About three more, above me. Then nothing. File attached, it is from the phone so not good quality. Sorry for my spelling.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: ok I listened three times and I'm not laughing. you can hear your keys, then your steps, then you stop and there's like three more, softer. but also what's that hum under all of it? it goes on and off. sounds like a fridge. is there a fridge up there?

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: There isn't a fridge on that floor. At the stairwell end of 8 it is the bin store. Bins, a mop sink, a light that does not work. I pass it every night. I don't know what the hum is. Maybe the phone. I will ask the people on LowBand tomorrow, they know about sound.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Thank you. Two requests: 1. please send me the original file, not the version the board compressed; 2. note your exact start point. From 8 to 6 is 2 flights, 38 steps. If you stopped at 7 you took 19. I would like to count everything audible on the file and compare. No conclusions until then.

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: Headphones on, lights on (all of them, obviously). The three extra steps are there. They sound lighter than yours (I'd draw them in pencil, yours in pen). They also sound like they're on concrete, not inside a phone. I'm not saying what that means. I'm saying I'm sleeping with the hallway light on.

units.author: dc_8_benedikt
units.text: Tobin, the original is on my old phone in the van, I will get it. I started at the door of 8, by the bin store, and stopped on 7 at the window. I counted to five and walked on. When I got to 6 the light came back on. Nobody passed me. I would have felt it.

units.title: Brackwater knocks: times so far, all nights
units.author: dunlin_rec

edit.note: edited: wrong time on night one
edit.text: Summary, for anyone joining. Night one (posted day 2): five knocks, west side, 600 m from the dam gate, at 02:40, not 03:40 as I first wrote. The handheld that stamped that file was still on summer time; I've checked it against the main recorder. Night three (fog, east ride footpath): three knocks at 02:41. Nothing on the clear night between. So both nights are 02:40, give or take a minute. Make of it what you will.

units.text: Summary, for anyone joining. Night one (posted day 2): five knocks, west side, 600 m from the dam gate, at 03:40. Night three (fog, east ride footpath): three knocks at 02:41. Nothing on the clear night between. Kit and gain as before. I'll keep the same pattern of nights and post each one, with or without anything on it. Make of it what you will.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so wait, with the edit that's 02:40 on both nights?? that's the same minute. that's either really interesting or really boring and I genuinely can't tell which. also a recorder still on summer time is the most LowBand thing I've ever read, mine was on the wrong year until last week

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Well caught on the clock. Same minute on two nights is the strongest argument yet for something on a timer: valve exercising, a pump schedule, an irrigation cycle at the estate nursery, a farm's frost protection. Machines keep appointments. Deer don't. Worth asking the water company and the estate for any scheduled equipment around 02:40.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Agreed, Hollis, which is why I wrote to the water company yesterday. I'll add the estate nursery, I hadn't thought of frost protection. The direction is still the awkward part: north, into the trees, with no plant there that I know of. But I'm willing to be wrong about what's in the trees. That's why I'm asking.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Told you. Timer. There's a pump somewhere in those woods with an appointment at 02:40 and nobody's looked at it since it was installed. Find the pump.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: Thank you for keeping to the path. It's deer. Stags clash in the east wood, the sound carries in still air, and you hear the last of the rut at odd hours when there's been disturbance in the day. And there has been, with the transformer works on Reservoir Lane. You'll not get a timetable out of deer, but you'll get a lot of noise.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thank you, I'll keep to the path. On the deer: I'd genuinely like it to be deer, and I've got rut recordings from three years to compare. Antler clashes come in rattling bursts, irregular, usually with grunting. These are single, evenly spaced and dull. But the rut being nearly over is a fair point about how quiet it should be.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so spectrogram for the fog night is up (with arrows, sorry). less above 2 kHz than the first night, which Hollis says is path length not fog, fine. peak around 900 Hz again. same shape, just further away. the third knock is weaker than the other two, like it's tailing off. typo fixed above, it's kHz not KHz

units.title: Fog week: recording etiquette
units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Housekeeping for fog week. 1. Post raw files, not phone recordings of your speakers. 2. Say where you were, including whether you had permission. The Brackwater estate has asked us, politely, to stop leaving gates open. 3. No trespass on reservoir or harbour property. 4. 'Spooky' is not a description. Tell me the frequency, the duration and what else you could hear.

units.author: hobby_tapeloop
units.text: Thank you for the reminder. Might I ask, as someone who is not very good with the forum, how one posts a 'raw file' from a cassette? I have been holding my microphone up to the tape machine. I suspect from your first point that this is not ideal. Regards, Ned

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Ned, you're forgiven forever. Run a cable from the tape machine's line out into a recorder or computer line in, set levels so the loudest part peaks below zero, and record. No microphone in the air. If you don't have the lead, the archivist has a box of them and will post you one. We'd love the dam tape.

units.title: Dogs won't do the back corridor after 2
units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Small thing from the kennel, curious if anyone has ideas. We walk the boarders out the back corridor to the yard. Before 2am, no trouble. After 2, tonight and the three nights before, they won't do it. Biscuit, an old beagle cross, sat at the corridor door at 02:15 and wouldn't move for lead or chicken. Juno pulled back to the front run. The corridor's empty. Lights on.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Dogs know things we don't, but mostly what they know is smells. After 2 the heating cycles off in most buildings and the air changes direction. Something in a vent, or a mouse, or the cleaner's spray. I'd sniff around that door like a fool, Jo. I pass your town Thursday, I'll bring coffee.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: I like that, Merle. The heating does go to night mode at 2, now you say it. I sniffed. It smells of dog, disinfectant and the chicken I tried to bribe Biscuit with. I'll ask Pete to look at the vents when he's in. Biscuit is now asleep on my coat, which I'm counting as a win.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Agreeing with Merle. Two practical checks, Jo: 1. Ultrasonic sources. Some pest deterrents, motion sensors and failing fluorescent ballasts emit high-pitched noise dogs can hear and we can't. If something switches on at 2, they'll avoid it. 2. A temperature drop at the far end. Dogs are sensible. Usually there's a reason, and it's usually boring.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Night two log, gate 7. 00:00 to 06:00. Monitor 6 clear all shift. Patrolled NE yard 01:00, 03:00, 05:00, nil found. Wiped the camera dome anyway. Left a note for IT about the dropped frames. Baker brought rolls at 04:00, poppy seed. That is the full report.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Poppy seed tonight because the first batch of sesame went on the floor, which only the bakery cat witnessed and it will not testify. Gate7 tells me nothing exciting happened on his monitors, which I'm told is the best kind of night in security. It's the best kind in baking too. Smells like warm crust in here, if anyone needs it.

units.title: From the overnight desk: how a story grows
units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Not aimed at anyone. I produce an overnight radio show, and here is what I've watched happen in three hours tonight. Caller one: a van parked by a lay-by, nobody visible. Caller two: 'like the van the man said', but now it's 'watching'. Caller three: 'everybody knows about the vans'. Nobody lied. Every story borrowed one detail from the last. That's not evidence. It's an echo.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Fair, and I'll put my hand up, my van's probably one of the ones that got borrowed. For the record mine is still an empty cab and an engine running, logged, nothing more. I didn't say it was watching anybody. It's a van. The most it's ever done is leak oil on my car park.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: This is good, Orla. There's a well-described effect in shift-work studies: tired people remember the shape of a story they heard better than its details, and fill details from their own night. So the stories converge. It doesn't mean nothing happened to anyone. It means a cluster of reports is a weaker clue than it feels.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Or the stories converge because they're about the same thing... You'd say that, though. Radio people always do. You decide what goes out.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Source? We do decide what goes out, yes, that's called a producer. Tonight it was a farmer's lost goose, a man who wanted to dedicate a song to his bus, and two people arguing about the best chip shop on the coast. Gilliver won. If there's a cover-up, it's mainly about vinegar.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: night five, Merle, I drank it slow like you said and it worked. callers: one woman whose smart meter 'is spying on her'. it isn't, it's counting kilowatts, which is boring spying. one man who rang to read me his meter, then his neighbour's, then the one on the church. and one dead air call, nothing on the line for forty seconds and then it went. happens.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Dead air is the overnight producer's oldest friend. Most of it's pocket dials, people who lose their nerve, and autodiallers testing lines. If the same number calls at the same minute every night, it's a machine. Count yourself lucky; ours has a man who rings at 3am to tell us the time. He's always right.

units.title: Lab nights: a list
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: tonight's all-nighter, in numbers: 3 energy drinks (bought from Taro, judged by Taro). 1 banana. 47 figures, of which 12 are good. 0 people in the building except me and the cleaner, who sings. 1 corridor whose lights keep switching on by themselves for nobody, which I have decided is the building's way of saying hello. hello building.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Lovely list. Gentle sleep-clinic advice: three energy drinks after midnight will add more 'something moved in the corridor' to your night than any building. Motion sensors are often triggered by warm air from heaters or by the cleaner's trolley two floors away. Also, please sleep. Twelve good figures is a good night.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: For the record I sold her the drinks and also gave her a free onigiri because she looked like a ghost. The cleaner who sings comes in for a coffee at 5. She says hello to the lights too.

units.title: Pick rate targets, a rant (break-length)
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: They've upped the target to 140 picks an hour on the cold aisle, which is where the frozen peas live, which is minus 20, which is where fingers go to die. The scanner beeps when you're slow. It beeps when you're fast. It beeped at me tonight when I wasn't holding it. I've named it Gary. Gary hates me.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Hospital equivalent: the trolleys are timed now. The run from A&E to X-ray has a target. I've never once made it, because Doris on reception always wants to chat, and a target that doesn't include Doris is a target I won't respect. Tell Gary to have a word with himself.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Our yard backs onto your loading bay, I can see your dock doors on camera 9. Somebody on your shift stands outside door 4 every night at 03:00 for exactly eight minutes. Is that you? If it is, I've been watching you have your break for a month. Sorry. You look peaceful.

units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: door 4 at 3 is me and a cheese sandwich, yes. eight minutes because that's how long the sandwich lasts. it's the only time the yard's quiet and I can hear the motorway like the sea. now I know you're there I'll wave at camera 9. don't tell Gary

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Tape is still on the panel. Bed record now shows the new patient's name, so if it goes off tonight it should at least call the right man. It went once, at 03:02, and called his name, the new one, so Dmitra's half right already. I still owe nobody a coffee. Back to it.

units.title: Quiet night at the home (a small one)
units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: It's a quiet night at the home. Mrs A. is up and sitting in the lounge in her good cardigan, waiting for nothing in particular, and I've brought her tea in the cup with the roses. She says she likes the night because nobody asks her to do anything. I said that's why I like it too. I'm sorry, this isn't really a post. It's just nice.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: Don't apologise. Some of the best posts on here aren't really posts. The cup with the roses is a whole novel in four words. I hope she has a lovely quiet hour, and that you get a cup in the good china too when she's finished.
